title: OHTO.
subtitle: A Japanese stationery brand. A UI refresh of a site that still looked like the early 2000s.

glance.Problem: OHTO's website looked dated, roughly early 2000s.
glance.Contribution: Personal project: research, competitive analysis, sketches, wireframes and hi-fi comps in Figma.
glance.Outcome: A contemporary hi-fi redesign that follows the wireframe structure and draws colors from the current site.

sections.label: Overview
sections.heading: A stationery brand I use every day.
paras: OHTO makes unique pens, mechanical pencils, 3-in-1 multi-pens, and other stationery. I use the products daily but bought them through third-party sellers, so I had never visited the company's site.
When I did, it looked dated, roughly early 2000s, so I set out to refresh it.

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: How similar e-commerce sites are built.
paras: I surveyed UI patterns across e-commerce sites in the same category.

sections.label: Competitive analysis
sections.heading: Standard structures, dated details.
paras: I compared three similar brands. Most e-commerce sites share standard structures, and several dated elements, especially search and icons, were common on the weaker sites.

sections.label: Sketches
sections.heading: Lead with the product.
paras: I focused on the hero image, since OHTO's products are large in scale, and on showcasing the technology the pens use.

sections.label: Wireframes
sections.heading: Grayscale layouts on a 4px baseline grid.
paras: The wireframes carry the flow from the sketches.

sections.label: Hi-fi composition
sections.heading: A contemporary style.
paras: High-fidelity mockups follow the wireframe structure and draw colors from the current site, aiming for a contemporary style. The final comps are shown above.
